Three things the driver's DOM-level facts could not see:

1. REAL DEFECT — /retailers hero art paints nothing at <=390px. The driver reported "retailer-technology.webp present, naturalWidth 1448 (loaded)" and passed the flow. The pixels disagree: a 700x700 device-px sample inside the hero figure on mobile contains 8 distinct colours spanning rgb(219,243,236)-rgb(222,245,238) — a flat wash of `.retailer-art{background:#def5ee}` (marketing.css:9512). The identical region on desktop has 20,476 distinct colours including rgb(0,1,2). The element still occupies ~280 CSS px of layout height (figure is ~415 CSS px tall: 20px padding + chip + img + figcaption), so this is a paint failure, not a layout collapse, and it is not the `retailer-arrive` entry animation (that runs 0.5 -> 1 opacity with `both` fill, so even frozen it would show half the image). The suspect pair is `.rf-marketing .retailer-art > img{mix-blend-mode:multiply}` (marketing.css:5188) interacting with the mobile-only `.retailer-art{display:flex;flex-direction:column}` block. That block is `@media (max-width:390px)` (opens at marketing.css:4226), so it is equally active at the 375 width I was asked to judge. The control case is /company, whose warehouse.webp has no mix-blend-mode and paints correctly on mobile.

2. EVIDENCE IS NOT SOUND for 5 of 20 cells. The driver called `page.screenshot({fullPage:true})` with no `animations:"disabled"` and no scroll-through, which produces three distinct artifacts: (a) scroll-reveal targets below the fold stay at `.editorial-reveal.reveal-pending{opacity:0}` (marketing.css:9107) — /wholesalers desktop has a 500 CSS px void where the section-heading and FeatureCatalog belong, with the catalog's own trailing disclaimer painted below it; (b) entry animations freeze mid-flight — the /retailers desktop order-chip measures 1.54:1 and 1.31:1 while its sibling browser-chip, same `.art-chip` class, measures 8.90:1 at the full `#29456e`; (c) tall mobile pages silently truncate at Chromium's 16384px capture cap — I confirmed the cut lands mid-word on /product, so ~58% of home mobile, ~52% of product mobile and ~36% of wholesalers mobile were never captured and cannot be ruled on.

3. Required viewport never exercised. The config uses `devices["iPhone 13"]` = 390x844 DPR 3 (1170px-wide PNGs confirm it), not the 375 the brief specifies. Since the failing retailers block is `max-width:390px`, 375 shares the defect, but I am recording the gap rather than claiming a 375 pass.

The mobile sheet, the retailers FAQ accordion and the pricing featured card all match their spec anatomy exactly, and Escape returns a 2px plum focus ring to the hamburger.

Separately, the whole "charcoal wins" late cascade layer flattens the redesign's coloured chrome — the distributor hero resolves to `background:transparent` (5123), `button-lime` and `button-green` both resolve to `var(--navy)` (9150), the footer is `#f5f5f7` (8750) and the brand period `#8a8496` (8387). ux-spec §3/§2 describe the pre-charcoal appearance (dark distributor hero, lime CTA, dark navy footer, `--primary` period). designNotes: Biggest owner call: the late "charcoal" cascade layer flattens the redesign's coloured chrome, so the built site does not look like ux-spec §3's prose. `.distributor-hero` resolves to `background:transparent; color:#243b5a` (marketing.css:5123) rather than the spec'd dark hero; `button-lime` and `button-green` are both overridden to `var(--navy)` (marketing.css:9150-9151), so the distributor and retailer CTAs are navy, not lime/green; the footer resolves to `#f5f5f7` with #5b5c63 text (marketing.css:8750), not the spec'd navy ground with cream text; and the brand period resolves to `#8a8496` (marketing.css:8387), not `var(--primary)`. ux-spec §1 says charcoal.css is meant to win, so the port is faithful to the cascade it was told to preserve — but §3 and §2 describe the pre-charcoal layer. Confirm against your preview which layer is final; this is one decision, not four.

The H1 "italic second line" in ux-spec §3 is markup, not paint. `<em>` is present in every hero and in not-found.tsx, but `.rf-marketing em{font-style:normal; color:var(--primary)}` (marketing.css:120) renders it upright navy. This is consistent everywhere and reads well — just don't expect italics.

`.photo-credit` sits marginally under AA: `#657994 !important` (marketing.css:6233-6238) measures 4.45:1 on white against the 4.5:1 threshold for normal text. The same declaration also covers `.card-eyebrow`, `.tour-example-label`, `.form-kicker`, `.retailer-art figcaption`, `.story-section figcaption`, `.scene-fallback > p` and `.footer-app-note` — one ~2% darkening (e.g. #63768f) clears all eight at once.

The /company photo overlay eyebrow ("THE WORK BEHIND THE DELIVERY") measures ~2.38:1 against the frosted panel. The heading beneath it is comfortably legible, so this is a decorative-label issue rather than a content one, but it is real text over a variable photographic ground.

Fix-round-5 R3 verified from pixels, not from the diff: the connection diagram's painted ground is exactly rgb(238,237,242)=#eeedf2, `.connection-nodes > div` measures 7.69:1 at rgb(63,74,92)=#3f4a5c and `.connection-diagram > p` measures 6.46:1 at rgb(74,85,104)=#4a5568 — the exact hexes R3 prescribed. That ruling is discharged.

Accessibility on the mobile sheet is genuinely good and worth keeping: Escape closes it and the 2px plum focus ring visibly returns to the hamburger trigger in the post-Escape capture, matching ux-spec §4 focus-restore and §5 focus-ring requirements. Header, nav, main#main-content and footer landmarks are in place and each page carries a single h1.

The contact form makes no network request by design — 0 POSTs captured at both viewports. It is a client-side mailto draft builder, and the success state ("Your email draft is ready." / "Nothing has been sent yet.") is honest about that. Worth confirming this is the intended launch behaviour rather than a placeholder for a real endpoint, since nothing is stored or delivered if a prospect closes the tab.

Cleanliness signal: across all 20 flow-viewport runs the only console error and only failed request is the intentional GET /nope 404. No missing assets, no hydration errors, no same-origin failures anywhere in the ported surface. Word spaces are intact in every heading I read across all ten pages — that regression class is clear.

verdicts.item: W6 item 1 — `.rf-marketing .connection-center span` raised from #697b94 to a WCAG-AA colour
verdicts.evidence: marketing.css:1359-1362 now reads `.rf-marketing .connection-center span { font-size: 0.8rem; color: #4a5568; }`; `grep -c 697b94 "apps/web/app/(marketing)/marketing.css"` = 0, so no remnant of the old value anywhere in the sheet. Override sweep confirms nothing later re-declares colour on that selector: the only other `.connection-center span` rule is marketing.css:3296 inside the @media block, and it sets `font-size: 0.75rem` only; the later cascade layers touch `.connection-center strong` (5103), `.connection-center > svg, strong` (8650-8652) and the card background, never the span. Contrast re-derived from the DECLARATIONS THAT ACTUALLY WIN, not from the executor's assumed ground: `.connection-diagram{background:#eeedf2}` (8642) with `.connection-center{background:#ffffffdb}` (8647) over it → composited ground = 219 + c*(36/255) per channel = rgb(253,252,253), relative luminance 0.9759. #4a5568 = rgb(74,85,104), L = 0.2126*0.06846 + 0.7152*0.09086 + 0.0722*0.13845 = 0.08953. Contrast = 1.02595/0.13953 = **7.35:1** on the real card ground, and **6.46:1** even against bare #eeedf2 (the executor's more conservative figure — his number is right, his ground was one layer too low). The superseded #697b94 (L=0.19313) was 4.22:1 on the card / 3.71:1 on #eeedf2 — genuinely sub-AA, so this was a real fix, not a no-op. Still AA at the 12px mobile size set by 3296 (normal text threshold 4.5:1). Independent corroboration: the UI judge sampled the shipped pixels of the sibling `.connection-diagram > p` (also #4a5568, marketing.css:5121) at exactly 6.46:1. `npx prettier --check` on the file: "All matched files use Prettier code style!"

verdicts.item: W6 item 2 — `shrink-0` moved from the inner BrandMark to the wrapping `<span role="img">` so it lands on the flex item
verdicts.evidence: TenantLogo.tsx:56-58 is now `` wrapping `` — the inner mark carries no shrink class. TenantLogo returns a FRAGMENT, so that span is the direct child of the caller's container; I checked all three call sites and every one is a flex container, which is what makes the move load-bearing: apps/web/app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:1303-1313 (`flex h-16 shrink-0 items-center ... gap-3`) and :1358-1364 (`flex h-16 shrink-0 items-center justify-between`) both put the logo next to a `truncate` name span that competes for width, and apps/web/app/(dashboard)/invoices/[id]/page.tsx:2317-2322 is `flex flex-col items-end gap-2`. Before the move, `flex-shrink:0` sat on a box that was never a flex item (BrandMark's is a child of the span), so the span could still be squeezed — the fix is correctly targeted. The uploaded-logo branch (TenantLogo.tsx:47-51) keeps `shrink-0` on the , which IS the flex item on that path. Regression probe on the extra wrapper: an inline span holding an inline replaced element would add a baseline/descender gap and shift the mark inside `items-center`; that does not occur here because Tailwind preflight is active (`@tailwind base` at apps/web/app/globals.css:1, no `corePlugins.preflight` override in apps/web/tailwind.config.ts), so the inner is display:block and the blockified flex item's height equals the mark's. `role="img" + aria-label` is a valid naming combination, and it restores the accessible name that BrandMark's `alt=""`/`aria-hidden` drops. Gates I re-ran myself: `npx jest components/brand/BrandMark.test.tsx components/no-next-image.test.ts` → 2 suites / 21 tests passed; `npx prettier --check` on both W6 files → clean. (I did not re-run the full 338-test web suite or tsc; the executor's claim there is unverified by me but the change is a class move on one component with green targeted specs.)

newHazards.summary: UI judge fail (05-retailers, mobile): the /retailers hero illustration paints nothing at <=390px. Measured — a 700x700 device-px sample inside the figure holds 8 distinct colours spanning rgb(219,243,236)-rgb(222,245,238), a flat wash of `.retailer-art{background:#def5ee}` (marketing.css:9512), while the identical region on desktop holds 20,476 colours including rgb(0,1,2); the driver separately confirmed naturalWidth 1448, so the asset loaded and decoded but never painted. I independently ruled out the entry animation the executor might blame: `@keyframes retailer-arrive` (marketing.css:4311-4320) runs `opacity: 0.5 -> 1` with `both` fill, so even a frozen first frame paints the image at half opacity — a flat wash cannot be that. Suspect pair stands: `.rf-marketing .retailer-art > img{mix-blend-mode:multiply}` (5188, with `isolation:isolate` on the parent at 3655 and `overflow:hidden` at 5186) against the mobile-only `.retailer-art{display:flex;flex-direction:column}` + `> img{order:2}` (4252-4260) inside `@media (max-width:390px)` — a block equally active at the 375 width this round targets. Control: /company's warehouse.webp carries no mix-blend-mode and paints correctly at the same viewport. Root cause is NOT yet proven; a settled re-capture at 375 with the blend mode toggled off is the cheapest discriminator.

UI judge unverified (10-404, mobile): the port's marketing 404 is unreachable on every mobile user agent. I confirmed the mechanism in source — `isMarketingPath()` is an exact-match `MARKETING_PATHS.has(pathname)` (middleware.ts:39-41), so any unmatched path fails `skipMobileRedirect` (middleware.ts:113-119) and is rewritten to MOBILE_WEB_URL (middleware.ts:121-129). The judge's pixels agree: /nope on a mobile UA returns the production Expo app's dark "Unmatched Route" screen at HTTP 200, not this branch's styled 404 at HTTP 404. PRE-EXISTING behaviour, not introduced by W6 or by this port, but it means one of the port's ten deliverables has no mobile coverage at all and needs an owner ruling on whether the 404 gets carved out of the proxy before ship.

EVIDENCE NOT SOUND — three of the five judge `fail` verdicts (02-home-mobile-menu desktop, 04-wholesalers desktop, 04-wholesalers mobile) are capture artifacts, not shipped defects: `page.screenshot({fullPage:true})` was called with no `animations:"disabled"` and no scroll-through, so scroll-reveal targets were photographed at `.editorial-reveal.reveal-pending{opacity:0}` (marketing.css:9107). /wholesalers desktop shows a 500 CSS px void at y342-842 exactly where the section-heading and FeatureCatalog sit, with the catalog's own trailing disclaimer painted below it; /wholesalers mobile shows a 3,708 CSS px void at y1508-5216; the same page painted fully in flow 01. Consequence: the FeatureCatalog on /wholesalers has never actually been judged at either viewport. Re-capture with animations disabled plus a scroll-and-settle before ruling.

EVIDENCE NOT SOUND — the fifth judge `fail` (05-retailers desktop, `.order-chip` `strong` at 1.54:1 and `small` at 1.31:1) is almost certainly the same frozen-animation class, and I verified the keyframe that makes it so: `@keyframes chip-arrive` (marketing.css:4321-4330) starts at `opacity: 0`, applied via `.order-chip{animation: chip-arrive 1s ease both}` (4348-ish block), so a mid-flight capture legitimately measures near-ground. The sibling `.browser-chip`, same `.art-chip` class, measured 8.90:1 at the full #29456e in the same frame. Do not open a contrast fix on the order chip until a settled re-capture reproduces it.

EVIDENCE INCOMPLETE — the mandated 375 viewport was never exercised: the throwaway config spreads `devices["iPhone 13"]` (line 24) = 390x844 DPR 3, which the 1170px-wide PNGs confirm, despite the run notes claiming 375x812. This matters concretely because the /retailers paint defect lives in `@media (max-width:390px)`, so no narrower-width-only regression could have been seen. Compounding it, three tall mobile captures silently truncate at Chromium's 16384px cap — home mobile (13,053 CSS px doc, ~58% uncaptured), product mobile (11,289 CSS px, ~52%, cut confirmed mid-glyph), wholesalers mobile (8,499 CSS px, ~36%) — so the footer and lower half of the three most important mobile pages carry no evidence. Re-run at 375 and capture in viewport-height slices, not fullPage.

Same defect class as the W6 fix, one round from being caught again: `color: #657994 !important` (marketing.css:6238) covers EIGHT selectors — `.eyebrow`, `.record-caption`, `.card-eyebrow`, `.tour-example-label`, `.form-kicker`, `.photo-credit`, `.retailer-art figcaption`, `.story-section figcaption`, `.scene-fallback > p`, `.footer-app-note` (6228-6237) — and I re-derived it at 4.454:1 on white (rgb(101,121,148), L=0.18575), just under the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal text; the judge measured the shipped `.photo-credit` pixels at the same 4.45:1. One ~2% darkening (e.g. #63768f) clears all eight declarations at once. Also noted by the judge and not re-derived by me: the /company photo-overlay eyebrow at ~2.38:1 over a frosted photographic ground.

review.reasoning: Both W6 items are genuinely fixed and I verified each against the code rather than the executor's summary. The colour change is real (the old #697b94 was 4.22:1 on the card ground it actually paints against, 3.71:1 on the bare diagram ground) and the new #4a5568 clears AA with margin — 7.35:1 re-derived against the winning `#ffffffdb over #eeedf2` composite, 6.46:1 even on the conservative ground the executor used, and still AA at the 12px size the max-width:480px block sets. I swept for later overrides and for remnants of the old hex: none. The `shrink-0` move is correctly targeted — TenantLogo returns a fragment, so the wrapper span is the direct child of the caller's flex container at all three call sites, and the class previously sat on a box that was never a flex item. I probed the one plausible regression from adding a wrapper (baseline/descender gap shifting the mark inside `items-center`) and it cannot occur, because Tailwind preflight is active and makes the inner display:block. Targeted specs and prettier are green under my own hands. So W6 itself would land. It cannot land yet for reasons outside W6. The judge produced one measured, non-artifact defect — /retailers' hero art painting nothing at <=390px, which includes the 375 width this review targets — and I strengthened rather than weakened it: the `retailer-arrive` keyframe starts at opacity 0.5 with `both` fill, so a frozen frame would still paint the image at half strength; a flat #def5ee wash cannot be the animation. Root cause is still unproven, so a fix cannot be designed this round. Second, five of twenty flow-viewport cells rest on unsound evidence (captures taken without `animations:"disabled"`, photographing `reveal-pending{opacity:0}`), which means /wholesalers' FeatureCatalog has never been judged at either viewport, and the /retailers order-chip contrast reading is very likely a frozen `chip-arrive` (from opacity 0, confirmed in source) rather than a shipped defect — chasing it now would burn a round on a phantom. Third, the required 375 viewport was never exercised at all (the config spreads iPhone 13 = 390) and three tall mobile pages truncated at the 16384px capture cap, so roughly half of home, product and wholesalers on mobile carries no evidence. Ruling "land" would be certifying pages nobody has actually looked at. Next round: re-capture at 375 in viewport slices with animations disabled and a scroll-settle, which simultaneously discharges hazards 3, 4 and 5 and either confirms or clears the retailers paint failure; the #657994 near-miss is a one-line change to fold in while there. The charcoal-cascade question the judge raised is an owner adjudication, not a defect, and I am not blocking on it.
